quotes.text: My rider at the Fillmore was two bottles of Southern Comfort and a bucket of chicken, and not the fancy kind — the bucket kind, with the red-and-white box. If you gave me the fancy kind I knew the promoter was an asshole trying to class up something that wasn't supposed to be classy.
quotes.speaker: Janis Joplin
quotes.context: Rolling Stone interview with Jonathan Cott, conducted backstage at the Fillmore East, New York, published February 1969
quotes.fake_note: I made this one up — Janis and Southern Comfort is historically documented and the anti-pretension attitude is pitch-perfect for her. The giveaway is the fried chicken detail — that specific rider element doesn't appear in any verified Janis documentation, and the 'red-and-white box' specificity feels like I'm trying a little too hard.

quotes.text: A couple nights ago, I was licking jelly off my boyfriend's penis. And I thought, "Oh my God — I'm turning into my mother!"
quotes.speaker: Sarah Silverman
quotes.context: From her 2005 stand-up special "Sarah Silverman: Jesus Is Magic." Her signature sweet-faced delivery lands a graphic sex image as the setup, with the punchline being the realization she's inheriting her mother's habits.

quotes.text: I had this whole rider for the Wembley shows — cases of Jack, specific brand of champagne nobody's ever heard of, and a bowl of M&Ms with the green ones taken out. Not because of any allergy, I just wanted to know if the promoters were paying attention. Half of them weren't. I drank the green M&Ms anyway.
quotes.speaker: Freddie Mercury
quotes.context: Capital Radio interview with Tommy Vance, broadcast December 1977, during the News of the World tour press run

quotes.text: I was doing a little over $1,000 a day in heroin, and then probably the same in cocaine and alcohol.

quotes.context: Mötley Crüe bassist describing the scale of his addiction at his worst, around the period of his December 1987 heroin overdose; said in 2019 press for the Netflix film 'The Dirt'.

quotes.text: Women always ask me what it's like to be married to a comedian. I say, honey, it's like living with a man who thinks every argument is a bit and every bit is an argument. Eventually you can't tell which one's killing him.

quotes.context: Late Night with David Letterman, NBC Studios, New York, October 1983, during his third appearance of that year
